items.title: 67426_Hayes Pillars oral history interview
items.q: Gus Perryman was crazy about the Scott Joplin tunes back in that era and he played those tunes even way back then.

ctx.x: And there was a band here named Floyd Campbell, that used to -- he and a promoter used to bring Louis Armstrong down here on Sunday, evenings Sunday -- Sunday afternoons to play at the Paradise Ballroom, with -- with Floyd Campbell's band. And they would pay him, I think, $100.00 to come down and play those three hours, you know. And go back to Chicago, see. In the meantime, Floyd Campbell had a piano player, that who had formerly played with me, with us
in Jackson, Tennessee, named Gus Perryman. And Gus Perryman was crazy about the Scott Joplin tunes back in that era and he played those tunes even way back then. Gus Pearman did.

And, the Fall of 1928, I'm just trying to think, where did we go then? I think the band went -- yes, after we finished on the boat there in 1928, had a little vacation in Chicago, that's where I told you I met Dr. Charles L. Cook and his band, at the White City? White City Park, at 63rd and South Park? He had a band of great musicians, he was well thought of at that time.
